# SK7001 — Cyclomatic complexity is over the threshold

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

The number of linearly independent paths through a member, from its control-flow graph.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.8 |

## Why

Cyclomatic complexity counts the decision points in a body, and it is the number that predicts how many test cases the body needs to cover. It is computed from Roslyn's `ControlFlowGraph` rather than by counting keywords, so a `switch` expression, a pattern with a `when` clause, a conditional access chain and a `&&` short-circuit are each counted the way the compiler sees them rather than the way a regular expression would. It is the least interesting of the metrics on its own — a long flat `switch` scores high and reads fine — which is why it defaults to `hint` and why cognitive complexity is the one the gate reads.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
// a member whose control-flow graph has 40 conditional edges
```

Write:

```csharp
// the same logic split across members, or expressed as a table
```

## When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. What it can be is *useless* — a threshold low enough to fire on ordinary code teaches people to switch the category off, which is the same outcome by another route. The default is therefore set well above the corpus's p99 rather than at the textbook number, and the threshold is an .editorconfig option so a repository can tighten it deliberately. Generated code is excluded from the rule entirely; doc 07 § Metrics keeps it in the aggregate numbers, which is a separate surface.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7001.severity`
- `dotnet_code_quality.SK7001.threshold (default 25)`
